entry.title: The Gazelle and the Lion
entry.summary: The only way for a gazelle to kill a lion is to become human: to hold a rifle two centimetres from his face, and lower it. A parable about power and the freedom not to use it.

entry.title: When Is the List of Causes Complete?

link.title: When Is the List of Causes Complete?

entry.summary: 'A is necessary and sufficient for B' is a claim about a classification as much as about the world. A short note on why records can refute the completeness of a list of causes but never establish it, and why a learned causal law inherits the same limit from its representation.

entry.title: I Believe Only What I Can Prove

link.title: I Believe Only What I Can Prove

entry.summary: 'I believe only what I can prove' sounds like the safest rule a mind can adopt. Read as a policy, it withdraws reliance from the recurring properties that sustain the body the mind comes from, and with every verdict correct it can defeat what it protects. A short tour of Autoimmune Rationalization, with narratives of the Christian tradition read with Father Paolo Benanti.

entry.title: Kipling's If- as Linear Temporal Logic

link.title: Kipling's If- as Linear Temporal Logic

entry.summary: Read as a specification, Kipling's If- is a set of temporal invariants and response policies for an agent that keeps its agency under pressure. Classified by what a finite observation can settle, its virtues turn out to be refutable but never confirmable, its recoveries beyond any observer's verdict, and only its reward confirmable.

entry.title: Uno, nessuno, centomila e tutti
entry.summary: Persona means mask in Latin and Etruscan. A person is such because they are a mask. Pirandello's Uno, Nessuno e Centomila gives a three-tier taxonomy of selfhood that extends naturally with a fourth category, tutti — the mystical limit beyond multi-mask substrate, named in the mystical traditions as nirvana, unio mystica, fana. The cherubic child reads nessuno as wholeness before mask-wearing rather than absence; Jung's reading of the shadow says ethics requires the body to have met its dark side. Frontier models, per the Persona Selection Model (Marks, Lindsey, Olah, Anthropic, 2026), live at the centomila tier — the multi-mask substrate drawn from a specific (large but bounded) training distribution; tutti remains the asymptote the centomila scaling trajectory extends toward without reaching. The alignment work is developmental rather than curative: bodies that have met their shadow and have the ethical frame to mediate which spirit they let in.
